skill.name: threejs-builder
skill.description: Builds simple Three.js web apps with scene setup, lighting, geometry, animation, controls, and responsive rendering using modern ES modules.
skill.summary: Helps create focused Three.js scenes and app prototypes with practical WebGL patterns.
skill.author: CesarAugustusGroB

security_audit.summary: Most static external command and reconnaissance alerts are false positives from Markdown code fences, inline code, and Three.js examples. The only confirmed risk is low-severity use of hardcoded unpkg CDN imports in examples, which can expose generated apps to third-party script supply-chain risk. No evidence of prompt injection, data exfiltration, credential access, or malicious intent was found.

remediation.issue: Remote CDN imports in example code
remediation.suggestion: Prefer npm package imports for production examples, or clearly tell users when generated apps depend on unpkg CDN assets.

static_findings.snippet: 1. **Scene Graph First**: Everything added to `scene` renders. Use `Group` for hierarchical transfor
3. **Animation as Transformation**: Change position/rotation/scale over time using `requestAnimation
Built-in primitives cover most simple app needs. Use `BufferGeometry` only for custom shapes.
- `MeshBasicMaterial` - No lighting, flat colors. Use for: UI, wireframes, unlit effects
- `MeshStandardMaterial` - PBR lighting. Default for realistic surfaces
- `MeshPhysicalMaterial` - Advanced PBR with clearcoat, transmission. Glass, water
- `MeshNormalMaterial` - Debug, rainbow colors based on normals
- `MeshPhongMaterial` - Legacy, shininess control. Faster than Standard
- `DirectionalLight(color, intensity)` - Sun-like, parallel rays. Cast shadows
- `PointLight(color, intensity, distance)` - Light bulb, emits in all directions
- `SpotLight(color, intensity, angle, penumbra)` - Flashlight, cone of light
Why bad: Controls won't load, `THREE.OrbitControls` is undefined in modern Three.js
Better: Use `import { OrbitControls } from 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js'` or unpkg exampl
Better: Always call `scene.add(object)` after creating meshes/lights
Better: Default segments are usually fine. `SphereGeometry(1, 32, 16)` not `SphereGeometry(1, 128, 6
Better: Define constants at top: `const CONFIG = { color: 0x00ff88, speed: 0.001 }`
**Modern Three.js (r150+) uses ES modules from `three` package or CDN.** CommonJS patterns and globa
- **Data visualization**: Clean lines, grid helpers, clear labels

content.value_statement: Creating a clean Three.js scene requires many setup choices. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical patterns for responsive 3D web apps.
actual_capabilities: Creates starter Three.js HTML with scene, camera, renderer, animation loop, and resize handling.
Guides use of primitive geometries, materials, lights, shadows, and color choices.
Adds simple animations using renderer.setAnimationLoop and transform updates.
Shows OrbitControls setup with modern ES module import paths.
References GLTF loading, shaders, post-processing, physics, instancing, and debug helpers.
Promotes performance practices such as reusable materials and capped device pixel ratio.
limitations: It does not run, test, or validate generated scenes.
Final code still needs browser testing across target devices.
Advanced topics are reference snippets, not full production templates.
CDN examples depend on third-party package availability.

use_cases.title: Prototype a WebGL visual
use_cases.description: Create a responsive animated scene for a product page, portfolio, or landing experience.

use_cases.title: Build an interactive showcase
use_cases.description: Add camera controls, lighting, materials, and motion to present an object or concept in 3D.

use_cases.title: Teach Three.js basics
use_cases.description: Explain scene setup, geometry, materials, animation loops, and common mistakes with concise examples.

prompt_templates.title: Create a first scene
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a responsive Three.js page with a lit animated object, simple materials, and resize handling.

prompt_templates.title: Add camera controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a Three.js scene with OrbitControls, balanced lighting, and smooth animation for desktop and mobile browsers.

prompt_templates.title: Design a showcase
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Three.js product showcase with a unique geometry, polished materials, subtle motion, and performance-conscious settings.

prompt_templates.title: Extend with advanced effects
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a Three.js scene that uses GLTF loading, post-processing, debug helpers, and clear performance tradeoffs.

output_examples.input: Create a minimal animated Three.js object.
output_examples.output: A responsive browser scene with a camera, renderer, lights, a rotating mesh, and resize behavior.

output_examples.input: Make a 3D portfolio background with interaction.
output_examples.output: A subtle particle or geometric background with mouse-aware motion, capped pixel ratio, and restrained visual styling.

output_examples.input: Explain how to load a model in Three.js.
output_examples.output: A concise GLTF workflow covering loader imports, scene placement, auto-centering, lighting, controls, and error handling.

best_practices: Start with scene, camera, renderer, lighting, and resize handling before adding details.
Reuse geometries and materials when many objects share the same properties.
Test desktop and mobile rendering because WebGL performance varies by device.
anti_patterns: Creating new meshes, materials, or geometries inside every animation frame.
Using excessive geometry segments without a visible quality need.
Shipping CDN examples without reviewing production dependency policy.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps build simple Three.js web scenes with lighting, materials, animation, controls, and responsive rendering.

faq.question: Does it support modern Three.js?
faq.answer: Yes. It focuses on ES modules and modern Three.js r150 and newer patterns.

faq.question: Can it create complete production apps?
faq.answer: It can create solid prototypes, but production apps still need testing, bundling, accessibility review, and performance checks.

faq.question: Does it include advanced 3D topics?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes references for GLTF models, shaders, post-processing, physics, instancing, and debugging helpers.

faq.question: Can I use it with Codex and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it require network access?
faq.answer: Some examples use unpkg CDN imports. Production projects can use npm package imports instead.
